definitions.gloss: adolescent delusions of grandeur, chuunibyou syndrome
definitions.explanation: A colloquial term for the tendency of early teenagers (around second year of middle school, age 13-14) to act as if they have special powers, secret knowledge, or a dark and mysterious persona. Used humorously and self-deprecatingly.

examples.japanese: ⟦あの→あの：00915_ano⟧⟦{子|こ}→子：09851_ko⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{中二病|ちゅうにびょう}だ。
⟦{中学生|ちゅうがくせい}→中学生：10973_chuugakusei⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{頃|ころ}、{中二病|ちゅうにびょう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦こじらせていた→こじらせる：22115_kojiraseru⟧。
examples.english: When I was in middle school, I had a bad case of chuunibyou.

examples.japanese: ⟦{黒|くろ}い→黒い：00588_kuroi⟧⟦{服|ふく}→服：00695_fuku⟧⟦ばかり→〜ばかり：02006_bakari⟧⟦{着|き}て→着る：00541_kiru⟧「⟦{闇|やみ}→闇：14528_yami⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{力|ちから}→力：01661_chikara⟧」⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦か→か：09473_ka⟧⟦{言|い}っ→言う：00515_iu⟧てた⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、⟦まさに→まさに：00270_masani⟧{中二病|ちゅうにびょう}だった。
examples.english: Always wearing black and talking about 'the power of darkness' — that was peak chuunibyou.

notes:
{中二病|ちゅうにびょう} literally means "second-year-of-middle-school disease." It was coined by radio personality {伊集院光|いじゅういんひかる} in the late 1990s.

Typical symptoms include:
- Pretending to have supernatural powers or a hidden identity
- Adopting a dark, edgy persona
- Using grandiose or foreign-sounding phrases
- Rejecting mainstream things as "for ordinary people"

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {中二病|ちゅうにびょう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦こじらせる→こじらせる：22115_kojiraseru⟧ (have a severe case of chuunibyou)
- {中二病|ちゅうにびょう}⟦{全開|ぜんかい}→全開：29588_zenkai⟧ (full-on chuunibyou)
- {黒歴史|くろれきし} (dark history — embarrassing past behavior, often related to chuunibyou)

The term has become widely known through anime and internet culture, and most adults look back on their own {中二病|ちゅうにびょう} phase with embarrassment.
